title: II Samuel: A New Translation with Introduction, Notes, and Commentary (The Anchor Bible, vol. 9)
author: P. Kyle McCarter Jr.
allowedUseNotes: Modern copyrighted critical commentary. Project stores only its own summary/paraphrase of McCarter's discussion, with a single short attributed quotation (under 15 words) of his own stated conclusion; no reproduction of his translation, textual notes, or broader commentary.
summary: McCarter's Anchor Bible commentary on 2 Samuel, a standard modern critical reference for the book. On 2 Samuel 1:1-16, McCarter notes the episode's structural resemblance to the messenger scene at 1 Samuel 4:12-17 (the fugitive who brings news of a battlefield disaster) and treats the Amalekite's claim to have killed Saul as fundamentally unresolved by the narrative itself: commenting on whether David was taken in by the messenger's story, McCarter writes that '[w]hether David was deceived or not, we cannot tell' (McCarter, II Samuel, p. 63). This project cites McCarter for that narrower, agnostic point — that a leading modern critical commentary treats the reliability question as genuinely open in the text rather than as a settled harmonization problem — rather than for adopting either of the two more specific scholarlyViews (outright fabrication vs. looter's embellishment of a genuine find) surfaced from the two public-domain commentaries also cited on this claim (Keil & Delitzsch 1866; Gill's Exposition 1748-63). Coverage extended (2026-08-11, queue #20a) to 2 Samuel 3-4: McCarter's introduction and running commentary treat this material as part of the same 'History of David's Rise'/apologetic composition he names and argues for at length in his own 1980 Journal of Biblical Literature article 'The Apology of David' (cited on its own terms as source card mccarter-1980-apology-of-david) — 2 Samuel 3's account of Abner's death (3:26-30, 36-37) and 2 Samuel 4's account of Ish-bosheth's assassination (4:1-12) are, on this reading, two more episodes in the same defensive pattern the Nabal, Saul, and Ziklag-messenger episodes already establish. This general-framing extension is what supports claim-public-response's apologia scholarlyView; it is cited there. A secondary web-search pass in this same session could not page-verify a specific McCarter quotation naming Joab's rival-command motive for killing Abner (claim-abner-killing), the political meaning of Abner's approach to Rizpah (claim-abner-break), or McCarter's own preferred reading of the 2 Samuel 4:6 MT/LXX textual crux (claim-ish-bosheth-assassination) — for those three narrower points, named attribution is carried instead by other, independently page-verifiable sources added in the same pass (Matthew Henry's commentary for the rival-elimination reading; Keil & Delitzsch's commentary, already covering 1 Samuel 31/2 Samuel 1, now extended to 2 Samuel 3-4, for the Rizpah/throne-claim reading and the MT/LXX crux) rather than forcing an unverified McCarter attribution onto them.
